item.title: Writing an Incident Report
item.description: Describe how a spill interrupted a library event, document what people observed and did, and explain what staff changed afterward.

children.definition: An accidental release of liquid, or the liquid left where it was released.
children.example: A spill beside the refreshments station interrupted the library's evening talk.

children.definition: An object or uneven part of a surface that someone could trip over.
children.example: The report identified the curled edge of the mat as a trip hazard on the way to the side exit.
children.translation_ru: предмет или неровность, из-за которых можно споткнуться
children.translation_uz: odam qoqilib ketishi mumkin boʻlgan buyum yoki notekis joy

children.definition: A temporary stop in an activity that has already begun.
children.example: The interruption began halfway through the library talk, when the host asked the speaker to stop.

children.definition: What people do in the first moments after something happens to deal with the situation.
children.example: As part of the immediate response, the host asked visitors to stay seated while an usher kept people away from the wet area.

children.definition: An official list where an organisation keeps basic details of unexpected events that have been reported.
children.example: The supervisor added an entry to the incident register with the date, location and reference for the full report.

children.definition: A detail or circumstance that helped bring about an event but may have been only one of its causes.
children.example: The supervisor identified the position of the drinks tray near the edge of the refreshments table as a contributing factor.

children.definition: The order in which things happened, from the first to the last.
children.example: The sequence of events showed that the jug tipped over before the host stopped the talk.

children.definition: A step taken after a problem to deal with what caused it and make it less likely to happen again.
children.example: As a corrective action, the events coordinator moved the drinks station into an alcove before the next talk.

children.definition: The level of seriousness or impact at which an organisation requires staff to report an event formally.
children.example: The spill met the library's reporting threshold because it forced staff to stop a public event.
children.translation_ru: порог, при достижении которого о происшествии нужно официально сообщить
children.translation_uz: hodisa haqida rasmiy xabar berish majburiy boʻladigan daraja

children.definition: A detail that someone noticed personally while present.
children.example: The usher's firsthand observation was that liquid was already spreading across the aisle when she entered the room.

children.definition: The person responsible for overseeing staff and operations during a particular period of work.
children.example: The host notified the duty supervisor, who asked the usher to describe what she had seen.

children.definition: The specific point at which something happened, usually given as a clock reading.
children.example: The host estimated the time of occurrence as 18:12, the time he saw on the clock just after the jug tipped over.

children.definition: The length of time that an event or activity lasts.
children.example: The host entered eight minutes as the duration of the interruption, from the moment the speaker stopped until the talk resumed.

children.definition: An examination of a place or equipment to identify anything that could cause harm.
children.example: During the safety inspection before the next talk, the supervisor checked that the relocated drinks station left enough room for people to walk past.
